voys.title: Step by step: connect Voys
voys.intro: You need a Voys account with at least one phone number. It takes about ten minutes.
portal: Sign in at freedom.voys.nl and open Admin → VoIP trunks. Click Add.
Description: for example "Kiestoon". Voys also uses this as the outgoing name.
Number of lines: the maximum number of simultaneous calls. Internal number: a free three-digit number, for example 900.
Call permissions: only allow the destinations you really need (for example the Netherlands and Europe). This limits damage if something goes wrong.
Turn on "Use the caller ID of the trunk", so the number Kiestoon sends is shown. Kiestoon only sends numbers that are yours.
Save. Voys now shows the Account ID and the password: you need both in Kiestoon.
Open Advanced (SIP) settings and set the CLI header to Remote-Party-ID. Leave the static hostname empty: Kiestoon registers itself.
Optional, more secure: under Extra security, only allow the public IP address of your Kiestoon server.
Open the call flow (dial plan) of each Voys number and send incoming calls to this VoIP trunk.
kiestoon: Provider: Voys (already selected). Host ha.voys.nl, port 0 (DNS SRV), UDP, codecs alaw,g722 and the Voys IP ranges are filled in.
Username: the Account ID from Freedom. Password: the trunk password. Leave the authentication username empty.
Caller ID: one of your Voys numbers, for example 0201234567 or +31201234567.
Maximum simultaneous calls: the same number as the lines in Freedom.
Save. Within a minute the status changes to Registered.
Inbound routes: add a route for each Voys number. Voys sends the number as +31201234567; Kiestoon also recognises 0201234567.
Outbound routes: add a route with the Dutch numbers preset and pick the Voys trunk.

Is Kiestoon behind NAT? Fill in the public address on the Internet access page (reverse proxy) → Network and NAT and forward the SIP port and RTP ports to the server. The Voys IP ranges are allowed in the firewall automatically.
troubleshoot: Status stays Rejected: check the Account ID and password. Copy the password again from Freedom.
Status stays Not registered: your network may block DNS SRV or port 6060. Set host sipproxy.voipgrid.nl and port 5060.
Incoming calls end up in the wrong route: set "Called number comes from" to To header.
The other side hears nothing or you hear nothing: almost always NAT. Check the public address and the RTP port forward.
A different number is shown: turn on "Use the caller ID of the trunk" in Freedom and check that the number is yours.
voys.terms: Voys supports connecting your own phone system with a VoIP trunk, but does not help with setting up the phone system itself. Voys' fraud detection blocks a trunk when it sees suspicious calls.

kpn.title: Step by step: connect a KPN SIP trunk
kpn.intro: You need a KPN SIP trunk (KPN EEN Vast / VoIP Connect) and a fixed public IP address for Kiestoon. KPN delivers the trunk; the settings come from your order.
portal: Give KPN the fixed public IP address of your Kiestoon server when ordering. KPN only accepts SIP from addresses it knows.
Note the SBC address(es) and the SIP domain from your order. Standard is SBC 213.162.171.164; with high availability a second SBC 213.162.171.180 is added.
Ask KPN to deliver numbers in international notation (+31...). That is the standard profile.
kiestoon: Provider: KPN SIP trunk (already selected). IP authentication, host 213.162.171.164, TCP port 5060, codec alaw and both KPN SBCs are filled in. Change them when your order says otherwise.
Caller ID: a number from your KPN number block. KPN does not accept other numbers.
T.38 fax: turn it on under Advanced when you receive faxes. KPN offers T.38 first and falls back to G.711.
Save, then add an inbound route per number and an outbound route with this trunk.
Firewall: allow the KPN SBC addresses on TCP 5060 and the RTP range. Kiestoon does this for the addresses in the trunk.
troubleshoot: No calls at all: check that KPN has the right public IP address of this server and that TCP 5060 is open.
Calls to KPN mobile fail: make sure no other codec than alaw is offered.
Wrong number shown: the caller ID must be a number from your KPN block.
kpn.terms: KPN strips P-Asserted-Identity and accepts only numbers of your own trunk as caller ID. Values come from KPN's configuration guidelines (2017); your KPN order always wins.

cheapconnect.title: Step by step: connect Cheapconnect
cheapconnect.intro: You need a Cheapconnect account with a SIP account (phone number). It takes about five minutes.
portal: Sign in to your Cheapconnect account and open the SIP account (the phone number) you want to use.
Note the SIP username (the number in international format without +, for example 31851234567) and the SIP password.
Optional, more secure: limit the account to the public IP address of your Kiestoon server and set a spending limit.
kiestoon: Provider: Cheapconnect (already selected). Host sip.cheapconnect.net, port 5060, UDP and codecs alaw,ulaw,g722 are filled in.
Username: the number of the SIP account, for example 31851234567. Password: the SIP password.
Caller ID: the same Cheapconnect number.
Save. Within a minute the status changes to Registered: Cheapconnect only routes incoming calls to a registered trunk.
Add an inbound route for the number and put the trunk in an outbound route.
Behind NAT? Fill in the public address under Settings → Network and NAT and forward UDP 5060 and the RTP range.
troubleshoot: Status Rejected: wrong username or password. Copy them again from Cheapconnect.
Status stays Not registered: check that outgoing UDP 5060 is allowed.
Incoming calls reach the wrong route: set "Called number comes from" to Request URI.
No audio: NAT. Check the public address and the RTP port forward.
cheapconnect.terms: Settings from Cheapconnect's SIP trunk setup page for Asterisk. The values in your own Cheapconnect account always win.

speakup.title: Step by step: connect Speakup
speakup.intro: You need a Speakup SIP trunk. Speakup gives you a login name, a password and the numbers of the trunk.
portal: Ask Speakup for the SIP trunk details: login name, password and the trunk numbers in 31... format.
Optional, more secure: ask Speakup to only accept your trunk from the public IP address of your Kiestoon server.
kiestoon: Provider: Speakup (already selected). Host sip.speakup.nl, port 5060, UDP and codecs alaw,ulaw are filled in.
Username: the main number of the trunk, for example 31201234567. Authentication username: the Speakup login name, when it differs from the number. Password: the trunk password.
Caller ID: one of the trunk numbers. In the Netherlands you may only show your own numbers.
T.38 fax: Speakup passes T.38 end to end. For a separate fax trunk use host t38-sbc.speakup.nl.
Save, then add inbound routes for the numbers and an outbound route with this trunk.
troubleshoot: Status Rejected: check the login name and password. Put the login name in Authentication username.
Incoming calls reach the wrong route: switch "Called number comes from" to Request URI.
No audio: NAT. Check the public address and the RTP port forward.
speakup.terms: Speakup does not publish a PBX manual. Settings come from Speakup interop guides by Swyx and Tuxis; the details Speakup gives you always win.

ziggo.title: Step by step: connect Vodafone Ziggo
ziggo.intro: You need a Vodafone Ziggo Zakelijk SIP trunk. Ziggo supplies a username and password per trunk.
portal: Note the SIP username (31... format, for example 31123450000) and the password Ziggo supplied. Leave out @trunk.sipnl.net.
Note the numbers of your number block, also in 31... format.
kiestoon: Provider: Vodafone Ziggo Zakelijk (already selected). Host trunk.sipnl.net, port 5060, UDP and codecs alaw,ulaw are filled in.
Username and authentication username: the Ziggo username. Password: the Ziggo password.
Caller ID: a number from your block.
T.38 fax: turn it on under Advanced when you use fax.
Save. The status changes to Registered. Add inbound routes for your numbers and an outbound route with this trunk.
Behind NAT? Fill in the public address, forward UDP 5060 and the RTP range, and only from the Ziggo addresses.
troubleshoot: Status Rejected: check the username (without @trunk.sipnl.net) and the password.
Incoming calls reach the wrong route: switch "Called number comes from" to Request URI.
Calls drop after some time behind NAT: check the NAT settings and the port forward.
ziggo.terms: Vodafone Ziggo does not publish a PBX manual. Settings come from Panasonic's Ziggo SIP trunk setup guide (2017); the details Ziggo gives you always win.

fax.title: Fax
fax.subtitle: Received faxes go to e-mail as a PDF
fax.emptyText: Send a number to a fax box under Inbound routes, then faxes to that number show up here.
fax.boxesIntro: A fax box receives faxes (T.38 or G.711) and mails each one as a PDF. Choose it as the destination of an inbound route.
fax.noBoxesText: Add a fax box for each fax number.
fax.emailsHint: Separate several addresses with commas (at most 10).
fax.keepDaysHint: 0 keeps faxes until you delete them.
fax.ecmHint: Turn off only when faxes from a certain sender keep failing.
fax.routeHint: Tip: switch on T.38 on the trunk when your provider supports it; it is more reliable than fax over G.711.
fax.sendEnabledHint: Users can send a PDF from the portal, and allowed senders by e-mail.
fax.numberHint: Shown to the receiver as the sending number and in the fax header.
fax.sendersHint: Only these addresses may send a fax by e-mail. Separate them with commas.
fax.sendPinHint: When set, the subject of the e-mail must contain this PIN as well.

send.title: Send a fax
send.noBoxesAdmin: No fax box may send yet. Turn on sending for a box under Fax boxes.
send.noBoxes: Sending faxes is not set up yet. Ask your administrator.
send.intro: Choose a PDF and the fax number. Kiestoon converts it and dials, and tries again up to three times when the line is busy.
send.tooBig: This PDF is larger than 11 MB. Make it smaller or split it.
send.queued: The fax to {{number}} is in the queue.
send.hint: You get an e-mail with the result when your account has an e-mail address.
send.emptyText: Faxes you send appear here with their status.
send.confirmDelete: Delete this fax and its document?

mail.title: E-mail to fax
mail.intro: Kiestoon checks a mailbox every minute and faxes the PDF attachments of allowed senders.
mail.deleteHint: Otherwise the mail is only marked as read.
mail.how1: Use a separate mailbox, such as fax@yourcompany.com.
mail.how2: Add the allowed senders to a fax box that may send.
mail.how3: Put the fax number in the subject, or mail to fax+0201234567@yourcompany.com when your mail server supports plus addresses.
mail.how4: Attach one or more PDFs. The sender gets an e-mail with the result.
mail.security_note: Mail that fails the SPF or DMARC check of your mail server is ignored, so a forged sender cannot send faxes.

phonebook.title: Phone book
phonebook.subtitle: Shared contacts for everyone, on the phones too
phonebook.search: Search by name, company or number
phonebook.calling: Your phone rings first, then {{number}} is called.
phonebook.emptyText: Add contacts or import a CSV file.
phonebook.importHint: A CSV file with a header row: name, company, work, mobile, other, email, notes (Dutch column names and ; work too).
phonebook.replaceHint: Otherwise contacts are added and duplicates are skipped.
phonebook.includeExtensionsHint: Colleagues appear in the phone book with their extension number.
phonebook.callerIdLookupHint: When the number of a caller is in the phone book, the phone shows the name.
phonebook.xmlHint: For Yealink, Snom, Grandstream and Fanvil, through provisioning.
phonebook.xmlAuto: Provisioned phones get the address of the phone book automatically at their next configuration update.
phonebook.ldapHint: For phones and programs that look up names over LDAP. Only reachable from your own network.
phonebook.ldapsPortHint: LDAP over TLS, with the certificate of the phone system. 0 turns it off.
phonebook.ldapAuthHint: Phones sign in with the provisioning user name and password.
phonebook.bindPasswordHint: The password is the provisioning password (Phones → Provisioning settings).
phonebook.importedSkipped: {{added}} contacts imported. Rows skipped because of a missing name or invalid number: {{rows}}.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.subtitle: CRM, API tokens and webhooks
integrations.tokensIntro: Programs use a token in the Authorization header (Bearer) to use the same REST API as this portal.
integrations.tokenOnce: Copy the token now: it is shown only once.
integrations.rightsHint: Never more than your own role.
integrations.readOnlyHint: The token can only read, not change anything.
integrations.confirmRevoke: Revoke the token {{name}}? Programs that use it stop working.
integrations.noTokensText: Create a token for each program that connects.
integrations.blockedRoutes: Tokens cannot manage users, tokens, webhooks, updates or restores, and cannot change your account.
integrations.webhooksIntro: Kiestoon sends a POST with JSON to your URL when something happens, such as an incoming call.
integrations.signature: Every request carries X-Kiestoon-Signature: sha256=HMAC(secret, timestamp + "." + body), with the timestamp in X-Kiestoon-Timestamp. Failed deliveries are retried twice.
integrations.noWebhooksText: Add a webhook to let another program know about calls, voicemail and faxes.

eventInfo.call_ringing: An incoming call rings on an extension (for screen pops).
eventInfo.call_ended: A call ended, with its call record.
eventInfo.voicemail_updated: The number of voicemail messages of a mailbox changed.
eventInfo.queue_abandoned: A caller hung up while waiting in a queue.

wallboard.title: Wallboard
wallboard.subtitle: The queues at a glance, for a screen on the wall
wallboard.levelHint: Share of today's calls answered within {{target}} seconds. The norm is {{norm}}%.
wallboard.offline: No connection with the phone system: the figures are not live.
wallboard.linkGone: This wallboard link no longer works
wallboard.linkGoneText: The link was revoked or replaced by a new one. Ask the administrator for the new link.
wallboard.emptyText: Create a queue under Telephony → Queues.

alert.abandoned: {{value}} hung up today, the limit is {{limit}}

wallboard.settingsSubtitle: Screens for the wall, thresholds per queue and who gets an alert.
wallboard.screensIntro: A TV does not sign in: you make a TV link with its own secret key, which can only show the wallboard and can always be revoked. Open the link on the TV, a Chromecast, Fire TV stick or a mini PC.
wallboard.noScreensText: Make a TV link for every screen on the wall.
wallboard.screenHint: The link works without signing in. Anyone with the link can see the wallboard.
wallboard.hideNamesHint: Shows only the last 4 digits of the number, for a screen visitors can see.
wallboard.newKeyConfirm: Give {{name}} a new key? The current link stops working.
wallboard.revokeConfirm: Revoke the TV link {{name}}? The screen stops showing the wallboard.
wallboard.alertsIntro: Who gets SLA alerts and how often. An alert goes off as soon as a queue is over one of its thresholds.
wallboard.alertScreens: On the wallboard and the switchboard
wallboard.alertScreensHint: A red banner and a red border around the queue.
wallboard.alertPush: Push notification in the mobile app
wallboard.quietHint: The same alert of the same queue is mailed at most once in this period.
wallboard.recovered: Also mail when it is fine again
wallboard.thresholdsIntro: Empty means not monitored. The target time is also used for the service level on the wallboard.

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.intro: Upload the firmware from the vendor once and choose the models it is for. Phones fetch it from Kiestoon on their next provisioning, so they do not need internet access.
firmware.hint: A .zip from the vendor is unpacked automatically. Maximum 1 GB.
firmware.emptyText: Phones keep their current firmware until you add one here.
firmware.versionHint: For your own overview, such as 96.86.0.70.
firmware.modelsHint: Only choose models this file is meant for. A wrong file can make a phone unusable.
firmware.activateHint: Phones of these models install it on their next check, usually at night or after a reboot. Another active firmware for the same model is turned off.

latest.title: Newest firmware
latest.intro: Kiestoon looks up the newest firmware of the vendor for the phone models in use and shows which phones run an older version. Roll it out with one click, or let Kiestoon do it every night.
latest.sourceErrors: Not every source could be reached:
latest.emptyText: Models appear here once phones are added.
latest.downloading: Downloading from the vendor; large files can take a few minutes.
latest.modeHint_off: Kiestoon only checks when you click Check now.
latest.modeHint_notify: Kiestoon checks every night and mails the notification address once per new version. You roll it out here.
latest.modeHint_auto: Kiestoon downloads new firmware every night and rolls it out by itself. Phones install it on their next check.
latest.catalogHint: Leave empty for the Kiestoon catalog. Grandstream is always read from grandstream.com.

ztp.title: Zero-touch provisioning
ztp.intro: A new phone asks the redirection service of its vendor where its settings are. Register the phone there with the address below and it configures itself out of the box, also outside the office.
ztp.yealinkHint: Yealink phones are registered and removed automatically when you add or delete them.
ztp.httpWarn: This address uses plain HTTP. Phones outside your network need HTTPS: turn on internet access or set a public address.
ztp.guidesIntro: These services have no public API. Sign in to the portal of the vendor, add the server address and import the MAC addresses from the CSV.
ztp.credsHint: Phones sign in with the provisioning user {{user}} and its password, as shown in the address.
ztp.serverUrlHint: Leave empty to use the public address of this server. Must end in /prov/.
ztp.yealinkEnableHint: Create an AccessKey and secret in the Yealink Device Management portal under API.
ztp.apiHint: Only change this when Yealink gives you another address.

speech.title: Speech
speech.subtitle: Text-to-speech and speech-to-text. Piper and Whisper run on this server; ElevenLabs adds optional studio-quality cloud voices.
speech.notInstalled: The kiestoon-speech package is not installed. Install it with apt install kiestoon-speech, or run the installer again.
speech.ttsIntro: Type the text of an IVR menu or announcement and Kiestoon reads it aloud with a natural voice. Download at least one voice per language.
speech.sttIntro: Voicemail messages are written out and shown in the portal and in the voicemail e-mail.
speech.voicemailHint: Adds the text to the voicemail e-mail. The e-mail can take up to a minute longer.
speech.sttHint: Larger models are more accurate but slower. Small is a good choice for 2 or more CPU cores.
speech.sample: Welcome. Press 1 for sales and 2 for support.

proxy.title: Own reverse proxy
proxy.intro: Use this when Kiestoon runs behind your own nginx, Traefik, HAProxy or load balancer, instead of the built-in internet access.
proxy.enableHint: Kiestoon then takes the client address and HTTPS from X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto, but only from the addresses below.
proxy.trustedHint: One IP address or range per line. Never add a range that clients on the internet use.
proxy.publicUrlHint: The address users and phones use, for links in e-mails and for provisioning.
proxy.notTrusted: A proxy header arrived, but this proxy is not trusted. Add its address above.
proxy.docs: Example configurations are in the manual under Own reverse proxy. Forward WebSockets for the browser softphone.
proxy.portalUrlHint: A second address for employees, for example https://voipcentrale.example.com. Point it at the same Kiestoon in your proxy.

metrics.title: Prometheus metrics
metrics.intro: Publishes calls, registrations, trunks, queues and backups at /metrics for Prometheus or Grafana.
metrics.allowFromHint: Optional: IP addresses or ranges of your Prometheus server that do not need the token, one per line.

sites.title: Branch offices
sites.subtitle: Connect branch offices with Kiestoon Edge: phones work through an encrypted tunnel, without port forwarding.
sites.hubText: Branch offices and linked Kiestoon systems connect to this system over WireGuard. Only this system needs a reachable UDP port.
sites.hubEnabled: Accept branch offices and linked systems
sites.hubEnabledHint: Creates the WireGuard interface kt0 and opens the UDP port in the firewall.
sites.publicHostHint: The name or IP address edges and other systems use to reach this system from the internet.
sites.portHint: Forward UDP port {{port}} to this system if it is behind a router. That is the only port that needs to be open.
sites.helperMissing: The helper service does not answer, so tunnels cannot be set up. Check kiestoon-helper.service.
sites.wireguardMissing: WireGuard is not available. In an LXC container, the host must have the WireGuard kernel module (or install wireguard-go).
sites.confirmDelete: Remove {{name}}? Its edge loses the connection and phones there stop working.
sites.confirmRepair: Create a new pairing code for {{name}}? The edge that is paired now is disconnected until it pairs again.
sites.emptyText: Add a branch office and pair a Kiestoon Edge (Raspberry Pi, LXC container or Debian 13 machine) with its code.
sites.portalUrl: Address of this portal for the edge
sites.portalUrlHint: Leave empty to use {{url}}. The edge must reach it once, to pair.
sites.codeText: Open the page of the Kiestoon Edge in the office (http://<edge address>) and paste this code. On a Raspberry Pi without screen, put it in kiestoon-edge.txt on the boot partition.
sites.codeValid: The code works once and is valid for 24 hours. It is shown only now.
sites.how1: Install Kiestoon Edge in the office: write the Raspberry Pi image to an SD card, import the LXC template, or install the kiestoon-edge package on Debian 13.
sites.how2: Add the branch office here and pair the edge with the code. The edge builds an encrypted tunnel to this system by itself; the office needs no port forwarding.
sites.how3: Point the phones in the office at the edge: SIP server <edge address>, provisioning http://<edge address>/prov/. The edge relays SIP and media through the tunnel.
sites.how4: Extensions, voicemail and all settings stay on this system. If the tunnel is down, the edge shows it on its own page.

federation.title: Linked systems
federation.subtitle: Link Kiestoon systems in different offices: one phone book, internal calls for free, busy lamps and queues across sites.
federation.inviteText: Creates a code for the other Kiestoon. Its numbers are dialled here with the site prefix.
federation.joinText: Paste the code the other Kiestoon created. Its numbers are dialled here with the site prefix you choose.
federation.hubOff: Switch on the tunnel hub under Branch offices to invite other systems. Joining with a code works without it.
federation.prefixHint: Digits dialled before a number of the other site, for example 8 + 201. It must not overlap with your own numbers.
federation.prefixJoinHint: Digits dialled here before a number of the other site.
federation.siteNameJoinHint: Leave empty to use the name the other system gives itself.
federation.urlHint: Leave empty to use the address of this portal. The other system must reach it to pair.
federation.codeText: On the other Kiestoon, open Linked systems, choose Join with a code and paste this code.
federation.confirmDelete: Unlink {{name}}? Calls, busy lamps and remote queue agents of that site stop working.
federation.emptyText: Invite another Kiestoon, or join one with its code.
federation.directDialHint: Numbers of this site that do not exist here can be dialled without the prefix.
federation.how1: The phone book of the other site appears here, with the site prefix. It updates every minute.
federation.how2: Calls between the sites go through the encrypted tunnel and cost nothing. The caller is shown with the prefix, so call back works.
federation.how3: Busy lamp keys can show colleagues on the other site (key value: prefix + number).
federation.how4: Queues can have agents on the other site, and Follow the sun sends calls to the site that is open.

sun.title: Follow the sun
sun.subtitle: Send calls to the site that is open now, each with its own time zone and opening hours.
sun.emptyText: Route a number to Amsterdam during Dutch office hours and to New York during American office hours.
sun.formHint: The first rule that matches the current time in its time zone gets the call.
sun.label: Label
sun.orderHint: Rules are checked from top to bottom.

cluster.title: High availability
cluster.subtitle: Two Kiestoon systems as an active/passive pair: the standby copies everything and takes over.
cluster.enableTitle: Make this system the primary node
cluster.enableText: Install a second Kiestoon with the same version, then join it as standby with the code this creates. The standby copies the database every few seconds and the recordings, voicemail and prompts continuously.

modeHint.vip: Both nodes are in the same network. Phones use the virtual IP; keepalived moves it to the standby within seconds when the primary fails.
modeHint.manual: The nodes are in different networks or data centres. You promote the standby by hand, and point DNS or the phones at it.

cluster.addressHint: The address the other node reaches this one on.
cluster.vipHint: A free address with prefix, for example 192.168.1.10/24.
cluster.warning: Calls in progress are dropped when the other node takes over, and changes of the last few seconds can be lost. Both nodes must run the same version: update the standby first.
cluster.code1: Install Kiestoon on the second system (same version).
cluster.code2: Open its portal. In the setup wizard choose Join an existing Kiestoon as standby node.
cluster.code3: Paste this code. The standby starts copying straight away.
cluster.waitingJoin: Waiting for the standby node to join.
cluster.confirmSwitchover: Hand over to the standby node now? Calls in progress are dropped. This node becomes the standby.
cluster.switching: Switching over: waiting for the standby to have the last changes…
cluster.confirmDisable: Switch high availability off? The standby node becomes an empty system again.
cluster.what1: Promote the standby by hand from its own portal when the primary is gone, with an administrator account of the primary.
cluster.what2: Updates: update the standby first, then switch over and update the old primary.
cluster.what3: Backups keep running on the primary node.

standby.title: Standby node
standby.subtitle: This system copies {{name}} and takes over when it fails. Sign in on the primary node to manage the phone system.
standby.promoteText: Use this when the primary node is gone. Sign in with an administrator account of the primary node.
standby.force: Promote although the primary still answers
standby.forceHint: Only when you are sure the primary will not run the phone system any more, otherwise both nodes answer calls.
standby.primaryAlive: The primary node still answers. Use Switch over on the primary, or promote with force if it must stop.
standby.confirm: Make this node the primary node now?
standby.promoted: Promoting… The phone system starts on this node and this page reloads.

theme.label: Theme
theme.title: Appearance
theme.hint: Light, dark, or follow the setting of your device. Saved on your account.

transfer.noCalls: No active call. Answer or make a call on your phone or the softphone, and it shows up here.
transfer.consulting: Calling {{target}}. The caller waits on hold. Complete the transfer or go back to the caller.
transfer.dragHint: Drag the call onto a colleague, ring group or queue. Or press Transfer and pick a target.
transfer.dragHintReception: Drag a caller onto a colleague, ring group or queue to transfer them. Or press the transfer button and pick a target.
transfer.pickHint: Pick a colleague, ring group or queue to transfer the call to. Esc cancels.

welcome.toggle: Create a portal account and send a welcome e-mail
welcome.toggleHint: The employee gets a link to set a password, the portal addresses and the details for a softphone app. No password is sent by e-mail.
welcome.needsEmail: Fill in an e-mail address to send a welcome e-mail.
welcome.language: Language of the e-mail and the account
welcome.confirm: Send a welcome e-mail with a new set-password link to {{email}}? An earlier link stops working.
welcome.sentCreated: Portal account {{username}} created and welcome e-mail sent to {{email}}.
welcome.mail_disabled: Account {{username}} is ready, but no mail server is configured, so no e-mail was sent. Give the employee the link below or set up the mail server under Mail.
welcome.mail_failed: Account {{username}} is ready, but the e-mail to {{email}} could not be sent. Check the mail log, or give the employee the link below.

setPassword.title: Welcome, {{name}}
setPassword.subtitle: Choose a password for your Kiestoon account.
setPassword.doneText: You can now sign in as {{username}}.
setPassword.invalidText: This link has already been used or has expired. Ask your administrator to send a new welcome e-mail.

phoneLink.waitingText: These phones fetched their configuration from Kiestoon but are not linked to an extension yet. Pick an extension and link them: Kiestoon writes the configuration and tells the phone to fetch it.
phoneLink.confirmDismiss: Ignore {{mac}}? It shows up again the next time it asks for its configuration.
phoneLink.noUserAgent: The phone did not say what it is.
phoneLink.seenFrom_one: Asked once for its configuration from {{ip}}.
phoneLink.seenFrom_other: Asked {{count}} times for its configuration from {{ip}}.
phoneLink.modelGuessed: Recognised from what the phone sent. Change it if it is wrong.
phoneLink.modelUnknown: The model could not be recognised: choose it.
phoneLink.adoptHint: The phone is not registered yet, so it cannot be told to fetch its configuration. It picks it up at its next provisioning check, or right away after a reboot.
phoneLink.adopted: Phone linked. It loads its configuration at its next provisioning check, or right away after a reboot.
phoneLink.resyncToggle: Tell the phone to fetch its new configuration now
phoneLink.resyncHint: Sends a SIP NOTIFY (check-sync) to the phone through the account it is registered with now.

resync.sent: Saved. The phone was told to fetch its new configuration; it updates within a few seconds.
resync.not_registered: Saved. The phone is not online with an account, so it could not be told. It picks up the change at its next provisioning check or after a reboot.
resync.failed: Saved, but the phone could not be told ({{message}}). Reboot the phone to apply the change.
resync.skipped: Saved. The phone picks up the change at its next provisioning check or after a reboot.

phoneLink.extNone: No phone is linked to this extension yet.
phoneLink.extNoFree: There are no unlinked or new phones. Add a phone on the Phones page.
phoneLink.confirmUnlink: Unlink this phone from {{number}}? It keeps working without an account until you link it again.

desktop.notReady: This phone system is not ready yet. Ask your administrator.
desktop.noFavorites: No favourites yet. Click the star next to a colleague or contact.

status.failed: Could not sign in to the phone line

call.title: Call
call.dragHint: Drag the call onto a colleague

desktop.queuesHint: Sign in or out. You can also dial *45 on your desk phone.
desktop.noQueues: You are not a member of any queue.
desktop.pauseHint: Stay signed in, but get no calls for a moment

settings.speaker: Speaker (calls)
settings.audioHint: Tip: let it ring on your speakers and talk on your headset.
settings.noHeadset: No headset found. Sound still works on every headset.
settings.headsetHint: Answer, hang up and mute with the buttons of Jabra, Poly/Plantronics, EPOS, Logitech and other USB headsets.
settings.headsetAuto: Calls go to this headset by itself while microphone and speaker are on System default.

info.testingHint: Testing gets new versions first. They can still contain bugs.
info.installing: Installing, the softphone restarts in a moment…

portal.title: Softphone for Windows
portal.text: Call with your headset from your Windows computer, with your colleagues, phone book and queues at hand. Install it, then link it to your account with one click.
portal.noInstaller: The installer is not on this server yet.
portal.codeText: If the softphone did not open by itself, enter this code in the softphone:
portal.expired: This code has expired. Make a new one.
portal.linkOpened: The softphone is being linked. You can close this page.

keys.oneType: All modules on a phone are of one type.
keys.maxModules: This phone takes at most {{max}} of these.
keys.hint: Click a key to set it up. Drag a key onto another to swap them, also onto another page or module.
keys.noModules: No expansion modules fit this model.

explain.park: Parks the current call; the caller hears music until someone picks it up at a parking slot (71-79).
explain.dnd: Switches do not disturb on and off (*76).

keys.accountsHint: Line 1 is the extension above. Add up to {{max}} accounts in total, for example a shared sales line. Put them on line keys below.
keys.templateLoaded: Template "{{name}}" loaded. Save the phone to apply it.
keys.intercomHint: How this phone answers intercom calls (*80 plus the extension, or an intercom key).
keys.icBargeHint: The intercom call is answered while the user is on the phone.
keys.icOnlyAllow: This brand only lets Kiestoon turn automatic answering on or off.
keys.icAkuvox: Akuvox: every incoming call is answered on the speaker, which suits a door or loading bay station.
keys.templatesText: A key template is a key layout for one phone model, including its expansion modules. Apply it to several phones at once, for example all reception phones.
keys.noTemplatesText: Make a layout once and give it to every phone of the same model.
keys.confirmDeleteTemplate: Delete template "{{name}}"? Phones keep their keys.
keys.modelFixed: The model of a template cannot be changed.
keys.applySubtitle: The keys and modules of the chosen phones are replaced.
keys.applyHint: Phones that are online fetch their new keys right away.
keys.applied: Template applied to {{count}} phones; {{notified}} fetched their new keys right away. The others pick them up at their next provisioning check.
keys.appliedNoResync: Template applied to {{count}} phones. They pick up the keys at their next provisioning check.

hostnames.title: Host names
hostnames.intro: Kiestoon can use one address for administration, phones and SIP, and a second address for the employee portal. The addresses come from Direct internet access or Own reverse proxy below.
hostnames.pbxHint: Administration, phone provisioning and SIP registration. Phones and softphones register with this host name.
hostnames.portalHint: Welcome e-mails, set-password links and the Windows softphone send employees here.
hostnames.portalSame: No separate address: employees use the PBX address.
hostnames.blockAdmin: Block administration on the employee portal address
hostnames.blockAdminHint: On {{host}} administrators only get the user portal (and the switchboard). Manage the system through the PBX address.
hostnames.onPortal: You opened this page on the employee portal address. Use {{url}} to change this setting.
hostnames.blockNote: Kiestoon tells the addresses apart by host name. To keep administration off the internet completely, only publish the employee portal address in your proxy or DNS, and reach the PBX address from your own network or a VPN.
hostnames.sso: Single sign-on: register both callback addresses at your identity provider (OpenID Connect). SAML always uses the PBX address.
hostnames.adminElsewhere: Administration is closed on this address.

journey.title: Call journey
journey.open: Show the journey of the call of {{time}}
journey.heading: {{from}} → {{to}}
journey.live: This call is still going on; reopen the page to see the latest steps.
journey.partial: Only the call record is available for this call (it is older than the journey recording, or its journey was removed after the retention period), so this shows the basics.

hangup.remote: Hung up by the other party

ai.title: AI summaries
ai.subtitle: Transcripts and summaries of recorded calls and voicemail
ai.needsStt: Turn on speech-to-text under Speech first: AI works on the transcripts it makes.
ai.intro: Transcripts are always made on this server by Whisper. The summary comes from a local model (nothing leaves the server) or from Claude in the cloud (only the text is sent).
ai.callsHint: Only calls that are recorded anyway. New recordings are handled in the background, newest first.
ai.voicemailHint: Adds a summary and follow-ups to the portal, the softphone and the voicemail mail.
ai.keepDaysHint: 0 keeps them as long as the recording.

engines.localHint: Runs on this server with llama.cpp. Free and private, but slower.
engines.cloudHint: Faster and better, with your own Anthropic API key. Only the transcript text is sent.

ai.notInstalled: The local AI runtime is not installed. Install or update the kiestoon-speech package.
ai.ram: Needs about {{gb}} GB of free memory while it runs.
ai.localHint: The model starts when there is work and stops again after 5 idle minutes.
ai.keySet: A key is stored ({{hint}}). It is never shown again.
ai.keyNone: No key stored yet. Create one at console.anthropic.com.
ai.cloudHint: Usage is billed by Anthropic to your own account. Audio never leaves the server.
ai.testIntro: Summarise a sample voicemail with these settings.
ai.running: This can take a few minutes on the local model.

errors.speech_not_ready: Speech-to-text is not ready: download a Whisper model under Speech.
errors.ai_no_key: The transcript is ready, but no Claude API key is stored.
errors.ai_not_ready: The transcript is ready, but the local model is not downloaded.
errors.no_speech: No speech was recognised in this recording.
errors.summary: The transcript is ready, but the summary failed.

reports.title: Scheduled reports
reports.intro: An overview by e-mail with the figures compared with the period before, and the figures per day and agent as a CSV attachment.
reports.noneText: For example a weekly overview every Monday morning.
reports.previewHint: With today's figures, as the mail looks.

covers.daily: Covers that day, compared with the same day a week earlier.
covers.weekly: Covers the previous week, Monday to Sunday, compared with the week before.
covers.monthly: Sent on the 1st; covers the previous month, compared with the month before.

mobile.title: Mobile app
mobile.subtitle: Kiestoon on iPhone and Android, with push notifications for calls and voicemail
mobile.intro: Employees link the Kiestoon app on their phone to their extension. The app rings like a desk phone, also when it is closed: the phone system wakes it with a push notification.
mobile.enabledHint: Employees can then link the app under My devices.
mobile.step1: Employees install the Kiestoon app from the App Store or Google Play.

hotdesk.title: Hot desk
hotdesk.hint: Anyone can log in on this phone with *55, their extension number and PIN (the voicemail PIN), and log out with *56. While nobody is logged in, the phone uses its own extension as a guest account. An extension is logged in on one hot desk at a time.

hotdesk.autoLogoutHint: At 03:00 everyone is logged out, so desks start the day free.

adminPw.confirmNew: Make a new password for this phone? It gets the new one on its next check.

quality.title: Call quality
quality.subtitle: MOS, jitter, packet loss and round trip per call, trunk and phone
quality.noTrunkCalls: No calls over a trunk in this period.
quality.noPhoneCalls: No calls on phones in this period.
quality.emptyText: Kiestoon measures every call from the RTCP reports that Asterisk exchanges with phones and providers. The first figures show up here as soon as a call has been made.
quality.chartHint: The shaded band is the poor range (under {{limit}}). Point at a dot to see its value.
quality.trunksHint: Jitter and loss: received by Kiestoon / reported by the provider
quality.rxTx: Received by Kiestoon / reported by the other side
quality.rxTxHint: Kiestoon measures the audio it receives itself. For the audio it sends, the phone or provider reports back what arrived. That tells you on which side of the connection the problem is.

causePhone.lossTo: Loss towards the phone (Wi-Fi or local network)
causePhone.lossFrom: Loss from the phone (Wi-Fi or local network)
causePhone.jitterTo: Jitter towards the phone (network of the phone)
causePhone.jitterFrom: Jitter from the phone (home or Wi-Fi connection)
causePhone.rtt: Long delay to the phone (remote connection)
causePhone.mixed: A mix of jitter, loss and delay

causeTrunk.lossTo: Loss towards the provider (internet line of Kiestoon)
causeTrunk.lossFrom: Loss from the provider (provider or internet line)
causeTrunk.jitterTo: Jitter towards the provider (internet line of Kiestoon)
causeTrunk.jitterFrom: Jitter from the provider (provider or internet line)
causeTrunk.mixed: A mix of jitter, loss and delay

quality.alertTrunk: average MOS {{mos}} over {{calls}} calls, the limit is {{limit}}.
quality.diagGood: The call quality was good in both directions.

diag.lossTo: The problem is on the part to {{where}}: audio towards {{side}} was lost. Check the network on that side.
diag.lossFrom: The problem is on the part to {{where}}: audio from {{side}} was lost. Check the network on that side.
diag.jitterTo: The audio towards {{where}} arrived unevenly (jitter). Check the network on that side.
diag.jitterFrom: The audio from {{where}} arrived unevenly (jitter). Check the network of {{side}}.
diag.rtt: The delay to {{where}} was long. This is usually a remote or mobile connection.
diag.mixed: The quality to {{where}} was poor, from a mix of jitter, loss and delay.

quality.stripHint: Each block is one RTCP report (about every 5 seconds). The MOS of the call is its worst direction, so you see what one side heard.
quality.settingsSubtitle: Limits, alerts and how long measurements are kept
quality.tested: The test mail is on its way.
quality.mosHint: MOS is estimated with the ITU E-model from jitter, packet loss, round trip and codec, on a scale of 1 to 4.5. A normal phone call scores about 4.4. Values over the jitter, loss and round trip limits show in red and tell where it goes wrong.
quality.ruleTrunkHint: The average MOS of the last {{minutes}} minutes is under the poor limit, with at least {{count}} calls.
quality.rulePhoneHint: At least {{count}} poor calls on one extension in the last {{minutes}} minutes.
quality.ruleEachHint: A mail for every call under the poor limit. Busy installations get many mails.
quality.ruleRecoveredHint: A mail when a trunk or phone is back within its limits.
quality.emailHint: Alerts always show on the dashboard and on the call quality page.
quality.quietHint: The same alert is mailed again only after this time.
quality.keepDaysHint: Older measurements are removed every night.
quality.notifyHint: Prometheus gets kiestoon_trunk_mos, kiestoon_call_mos and more at /metrics, for Grafana and your own alerting.

teams.title: Microsoft Teams
teams.subtitle: Direct Routing: Teams users make and receive phone calls through Kiestoon and your own trunks. Kiestoon acts as the SBC.
teams.restartNeeded: The Teams connection uses its own SIP port. Restart the phone system (Settings) to open it.
teams.connSub: What Microsoft needs to reach Kiestoon. The firewall opens the Microsoft 365 ranges by itself.
teams.enabledHint: Turns on the Teams connection. Needs Internet access with a public certificate used for SIP.
teams.fqdnHint: Must be on a domain verified in your Microsoft 365 tenant and covered by the certificate. Usually your Internet access domain.
teams.portHint: Separate from the TLS port of the phones. Microsoft only talks TLS.
teams.trunkHint: Teams calls to outside numbers use these routes or this trunk.
teams.cidTrunk: Caller ID of the route or trunk
teams.callerIdHint: What the person you call sees.
teams.maxSessionsHint: Written into the PowerShell script for Teams.
teams.ringBoth: New users: ring Teams and the desk phone at the same time
teams.ringBothHint: Default for new Teams users with an extension. Can be changed per user.
teams.bypassNote: Audio always goes through Microsoft's media processors (no media bypass). That works from anywhere and needs no extra firewall rules for Teams clients.
teams.hubsHint: Kiestoon checks each proxy every minute (SIP OPTIONS). When one fails, calls go to the next.
teams.cInternet: Internet access with certificate for SIP
teams.cInternetTodo: Turn on Internet access and "Use the certificate for SIP"
teams.cCert: Public RSA certificate for the SBC name
teams.cCertEcdsa: The certificate uses ECDSA; Microsoft needs RSA. Save Internet access again to renew it as RSA.
teams.cFirewallOff: Firewall is off: nothing to open
teams.cHubsOff: Shown once the connection is active
teams.cUsersSub: {{n}} Teams users; run the script after changes
teams.usersIntro: Link a Teams account to a phone number and, if you like, an extension. Calls to that number ring in Teams; Teams users dial colleagues by extension.
teams.noUsersText: Add the people who should call through Kiestoon in Teams.
teams.numberHint: The number this person gets in Teams. National numbers get the country code.
teams.extHint: Optional. Calls to this extension then ring Teams, and the person shows as this extension.
teams.ringModesHint: Teams only: calls to the extension ring only in Teams. Teams + desk phone: both ring, first to answer gets the call. Without an extension the number rings in Teams. Queues, ring groups and the switchboard reach Teams users like any extension.
teams.featuresHint: Call history, recordings, voicemail when nobody answers, queues and ring groups. Teams users call internal numbers directly and 112 always works.
teams.p1s: Add the domain of the SBC name in the Microsoft 365 admin center and create one licensed user on that domain.
teams.p2s: Every Teams user who calls through Kiestoon needs Teams Phone (in Microsoft 365 E5, or as an add-on).
teams.p3s: Turn on Internet access with "Use the certificate for SIP". Kiestoon then gets an RSA certificate from Let's Encrypt.
teams.p4s: Install the MicrosoftTeams module (Install-Module MicrosoftTeams) and sign in as Teams administrator.
teams.scriptIntro: Kiestoon fills in your domain, port and users. Run it once, and again after adding or changing users. It is safe to run more than once.
teams.scriptNote: Microsoft can take up to an hour before a new gateway or number works. The status on the Overview tab turns green by itself.
